Category: Humanoid character.

I'm planning out the full module for an elven ranger archer in a high-fantasy anime style, aiming for a rich but manageable scale, and working out the skeleton hierarchy with the hips as root, standing height, and facing orientation before building out the rest of the rig.

For the rest pose, I'm going with an A-pose variant: arms extended outward and slightly angled downward, legs set a bit apart. I want to lean into the anime aesthetic using toon-kit elements like cel shading, ink outlines, and anime eyes, plus a glow kit for effects like an arrow glow or gem, while keeping flat colors within the palette limit since cel paints don't count against it.

Now I'm working out precise height measurements for feet, ankles, knees, hips, and the pelvis/waist to build the body proportions accurately.

Continuing to define joint heights for waist, chest, shoulders, neck, and head, giving the elf an anime-style oversized head relative to body scale, with hair extending the silhouette slightly above the skull. I'm then laying out the spine skeleton as a chain of points running from the hips up through the torso to the chest, figuring out how many joints that produces and what to name each segment.

Now I'm building the neck chain from the chest top up to where the head attaches, then placing the head joint with a slight forward-up tilt so the head bone points naturally outward from the neck.

To avoid orientation confusion with local bone axes, I'll switch to specifying absolute model-space coordinates for everything, using the `bone` parameter just to attach parts without relying on local direction math. This is simpler and more robust than computing head.local offsets.

Now I'm planning the body loft from hips to neck using a series of stations with widths and depths—pelvis, waist, chest, shoulders, neck base—though I still need to figure out whether the loft cross-section is boxy or elliptical.

I'll just go with the default smooth shape rather than specifying sides, passing bone and color options to the loft and binding it to the hips and spine chain.

Now I'm sketching the ranger outfit as a separate garment layer over the base body: a forest-green hooded tunic, leather bracers, a leaf-motif chest vest, belt pouch, quiver, bow in hand, and a shoulder cloak. For appearance I'm thinking long silver-blond braided hair, pointed ears, and green anime-style eyes, keeping the palette in forest greens.

Now I'm figuring out how to pose the bow in the rest position -- holding it vertically in the left hand at the character's side within an A-pose, deciding how the limbs curve forward and where the string sits relative to the body.

Working out the arm geometry next: setting shoulder positions, segment lengths for upper arm, forearm, and hand, and the outward angle for the A-pose direction.

Building each finger as a short capsule chain rather than full joints to keep the rig lightweight, roughly 20 joints total for both hands. I'm working out the spread and palm orientation math so fingers fan out naturally relative to the forearm direction.

Setting up finger chains...

I'm working out the arm chain structure too, parenting each finger chain to its hand joint and figuring out the right point/name counts for shoulder-elbow-wrist-hand spans so the joints line up correctly.

Writing sweep radius values...

Still defining limb geometry...

Checking that the ankle region still sinks slightly below the ground even with its larger radius, since the foot sweep slopes toward the toe.
